correctness.rationale: For every integer rim r≥4 and positive conductances A,B, the pair/edge normalizations are explicit. The cut boundary has at least two rim edges, with equality for precisely one contiguous arc; L1 coarea reduces all scalar and L1 targets to cuts. Dihedral averaging preserves both means; triangle inequalities restrict every rim separation and give the explicit piecewise affine-fractional envelope. Each endpoint is saturated by the dihedrally averaged metric of an arc cut (or the full-rim cut), proving the same sharp constant for all metric targets. Algebraic comparison proves the full-rim phase threshold and the increment law; differentiation plus rounding proves the square-root asymptotic. The exact rational checker supplies finite supporting tests, not universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact arbitrary-metric nonlinear Poincaré constant for a natural wheel graph with two independent conductance parameters, its complete optimal L1 cut family, and a sharp conductance phase boundary constitute a full structural classification. The fact that all metric targets collapse to scalar-cut sharpness is nonformal: known natural bipartite graph families have strictly larger metric than L1 constants. The unweighted asymptotic adds a natural infinite-size benchmark.
